# CORAL contact observations

`coral.tsv` records actual source `touchEffects1` calls with a CORAL attacking segment.
Two source runs and the bundled JAR produce identical bytes.
All five compiled helper classes also match across both backends.
The fixture contains 169 cases, 510 snapshots, 341 explicit operations, and 11 discovered newborns.

## Comparison contract

This contract and its fixed ledger precede Rust replay.
Compare scalar, photo, gas, statistics, velocity, endpoint, color, reaction, identity, and RNG observations exactly.
Only organism fields `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the existing geometry allowance.
For finite geometry values, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Check geometric NaN classification and signed infinity explicitly.
No other floating tolerance or NaN substitution applies.
Preserve signed zero and full 32-bit ARGB values.
Immutable Java Color object identity maps to exact ARGB value semantics.

Only `input` G/N blocks and labelled construction recipes supply original genomes.
Never construct children or replacement organisms from later observations.
Discover newborns through actual object identity, regardless of duplicate or wrapped numeric IDs.
Preserve genotype identity through actors, newborns, saved references, and synchronous statistics.

## Source authority

The CORAL branch occupies `Organism.java:12743-13103`.
Its catalog identity is `JAVA-Organism-CASE-12743-1`.
The common recipient-energy death guard occupies `Organism.java:13106-13108`.
Its catalog identity is `JAVA-Organism-IF-13106-1`.
The helper invokes the actual private `touchEffects1(Organism,int,int)` through reflection.
It requires exact current CORAL ARGB before each invocation.
It does not copy contact, infection, transformation, death, statistics, or placement logic.

Nested source calls remain real calls, including `infectedBy`, `transform`, `die`, and lavender helpers.
Source death clears infected and saved references at `Organism.java:5211-5212`.
The snapshots therefore record null references after successful infection followed by death.
Infection counters and statistics retain the observable preceding event.

## Execution and inputs

Compile `tools/reference/CoralOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.CoralOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated profile arguments recorded in provenance.
The helper requires isolated home, temporary, and both preferences roots before simulation access.
It rejects existing output directories and writes the TSV with `CREATE_NEW`.
The existing runner bounds each process and cleans its owned process group.
No GUI window, source modification, global profile change, or network operation is required.

Each case resets source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive settings.
`INITIAL_ORGANISMS` is zero, and initial oxygen is `1000`.
Other initial gases retain source defaults.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`, and meta mutation is zero.
GREEN weight is seven; the other 45 selectable weights are zero.
The setup seed is `827364`.
Labelled settings and controls override these values explicitly.

Five supplied genomes use identities `g0` through `g4`.
`g0` supplies the attacker, `g1` the recipient, and `g2` a separate selector/blocker.
`g3` supplies an independent infection code; `g4` is an actual clone of `g0`.
Recipes for `g0..g3` remain explicit; the `g4` recipe remains `clone:g0`.
Full input G/N blocks record every supplied property and gene field.
The attacker initially has CORAL, and the recipient initially has GREEN.
Most cases then set the recipient's current phenotype independently from its gene.

Three real source organisms are pasted and added in selector, victim, killer order.
The selector occupies `(1000,1000)`, the attacker `(3500,3500)`, and the recipient `(5000,5000)`.
Protocol role `victim` always names the attacker.
Protocol role `killer` always names the recipient.
Protocol role `selector` names the independent blocker and selected organism.
These established role names preserve the existing strict dynamic observer contract.
A real separate selector avoids MainWindow callbacks.
Selection metadata remains a named source-only exclusion.

`build_tree` creates a real frozen JTS tree from an explicit actor-role list.
J records actual inserted bounds; Q records actual query order.
Newborns enter the real world list without entering that frozen tree.
One case explicitly rebuilds the tree after a shared gene edit.
All contacts use current segment zero on both actors.

## Covered scenarios

| Group | Actual source observations |
| --- | --- |
| Palette | All 46 base colors, 18 state colors, unknown ARGB, and translucent ARGB. |
| Eligibility | Plant, consumer, fungus, enhanced fungus, silver fungus, and overlapping classifications. |
| Energy transfer | Ordinary blocking and infectious, CORAL, or fungus exceptions. |
| Indigo | CORAL protection, ordinary penalties, partial payments, infectious bypass, and transfer asymmetry. |
| Shields | Normal 185 and weak 2220 thresholds, disabling classifications, exhaustion, and distinct dodge flags. |
| Dodge | Full, partial, insufficient, empty, negative, NaN, and zero-cost exhausted payments. |
| Neutralization | Attacker phenotype changes before remaining shield or conversion logic executes. |
| Special states | Protective inactivity, dormant spore six, injured bypass, and FRUIT warning then conversion. |
| Lavender | Enhanced amounts, cap ties, wrapping increments, partial payments, and attacker or mutual exhaustion. |
| Common guard | No-op colors, altruism, ineligibility, strict energy threshold, NaN, and existing corpse inputs. |
| Transformation | Below-one and equal-one energy, success, blocked failure, fallback placement, and legacy-ID exclusions. |
| Identity | Duplicate IDs, wrapped next ID, frozen dead references, shared gene edits, and fully mutated inheritance. |

The 341 explicit operations comprise 171 actual contact calls and 170 tree builds.
Eleven cases insert actual replacement children.
Failed transformation still kills the recipient without inserting a child.
Source RNG, gases, membership, counters, and synchronous statistics remain observable after that failure.
No inaccessible failed candidate is invented or retained by the helper.

The final two cases exhaust shields in active yellow fungus and dormant spore-six branches.
Both source recipients die without setting `_hasdodged`.
Normal and weak white shields separately retain their different dodge-flag behavior.
These cases extend the original corpus without changing its first 167 cases.

## Protocol and scope

Use the [shared dynamic TSV protocol](reproduction.README.md#shared-tsv-protocol).
The mode is `coral`.
K contact rows contain stage, `touchEffects1`, `victim`, and `killer,0,0`.
K tree rows contain stage, `build_tree`, `victim`, and the explicit inserted role list.
This fixture contains no Z direct-candidate rows.

Each actor snapshot contains all 154 organism fields and three genotype-reference holders.
Each world snapshot contains ten getter-style values and all 15 instance fields.
Each statistics snapshot contains all 52 fields and 49 public zero-argument getters.
Each genome observation contains 28 fields, including reference and gene-count identities.
Every observed gene contains all 40 source fields.
R records the following long, bounded integer, and raw double from a copied source Random.

D discovers newborns through actual world-list object identities.
H and G preserve genotype identities, including shared metadata and mutated genes.
Y uses the existing `observable` and `rejected-only` meanings.
Every Y in this fixture is `observable`; no rejected-only genotype rows occur.
No output G/N block becomes a construction recipe.

O `_world` and `_visibleWorld` remain named collaborator exclusions.
V `_visibleWorld`, `inCorridors`, `outCorridors`, and `_corridorexists` remain named UI or corridor exclusions.
These source values do not establish implemented Rust UI callbacks or transport.
All remaining fields, available genotypes, identities, tree queries, and RNG observations remain comparisons.

Schema checks validate field names, types, cardinalities, ordinal genes, commands, role tokens, references, and snapshot completeness.
They also validate selected outcomes directly from actual source observations.
The six negative guards cover four missing profiles, an existing output sentinel, and an escaping profile symlink.
All 74 original files retain their hashes, sizes, and modes.
All 27 prior TSV fixtures remain unchanged.

The initial private candidate used semantic roles `blocker`, `parent`, and `peer`.
Its helper, outputs, and receipts remain preserved.
Structured role-bearing columns map to `selector`, `victim`, and `killer`.
The entire original corpus matches under that mapping before the two final cases append.
Clade strings, numeric IDs, `_parentID`, biological fields, statistics, and RNG bytes remain unchanged.

One private validator assertion incorrectly expected infection retention after death.
Its failed receipt and script remain preserved.
Source inspection corrected only that validator postcondition.
The helper, observations, ledgers, comparison allowances, and published bytes did not change.

These observations do not execute complete frames, collision scheduling, every contact actor, UI callbacks, networking, or persistence.
They do not prove exhaustive branch combinations or full gameplay acceptance.
Rust replay and independent review remain separate evidence.
